records.mechanism: Active goal representations bias selective attention toward goal-relevant inputs.
boundary_conditions: Competes with stimulus salience and selection history.
Goal relevance is state/task dependent.
transport_limits: Do not infer active goals from exposure alone.

records.mechanism: Salience can change which attributes/options receive attention and decision weight.
boundary_conditions: Salience can be perceptual or economic and these should not be collapsed.
Choice context changes diagnosticity.
transport_limits: No universal conversion effect.

records.mechanism: Working-memory limits constrain sentence-processing performance as integration/maintenance demands increase.
boundary_conditions: Prior knowledge and linguistic structure matter.
Working-memory tasks do not provide a universal capacity coefficient.
transport_limits: Laboratory language tasks require cautious transport to naturalistic copy.

records.mechanism: Experienced processing ease can be interpreted as evidence about plausibility/familiarity when its source is not discounted.
boundary_conditions: Attribution of fluency signal matters.
Fluency can arise from perceptual or conceptual sources.
transport_limits: Do not equate easy reading with truth.

records.mechanism: Comparative message formats can alter attention allocation and message processing relative to noncomparative presentation.
boundary_conditions: Effects differ by brand familiarity, claim type and outcome.
transport_limits: Evidence base is primarily advertising.

records.mechanism: Self-relevance can increase the subjective significance/value assigned to information or outcomes.
boundary_conditions: Multiple identities and goals can conflict.
transport_limits: Self-relevance is not generic liking.

records.mechanism: Perceived similarity can contribute to favorable trust/source evaluations in some social-source contexts.
boundary_conditions: Similarity dimension, platform, product and source type matter.
transport_limits: Strongest support here comes from influencer/social-media literature.

records.mechanism: Relevant character-recipient similarity can strengthen identification with narrative characters.
boundary_conditions: Similarity type and narrative context matter.
Similarity is not identical to identification.
transport_limits: Narrative contexts only.

records.mechanism: Perceived descriptive norms can be associated with behavioral intentions, with distinct pathways from injunctive norms.
boundary_conditions: Referent group and identification matter.
Descriptive and injunctive norms must remain separate.
transport_limits: Meta evidence includes bounded health/social contexts.

records.mechanism: Implementation burden creates barriers after intention formation, increasing risk that intention does not translate into behavior.
boundary_conditions: Opportunity, habit, planning and motivation also affect translation.
transport_limits: Specific friction type and behavior must be observed or manipulated.

records.mechanism: Emotional appeal design can evoke goal-relevant appraisal/affective responses, but effect depends on the specific appeal and audience.
boundary_conditions: Different emotions are not interchangeable.
Appraisal and perceived relevance determine response.
transport_limits: No generic emotional-appeal coefficient.

records.mechanism: Comparative structure supplies explicit alternatives/reference context that enables relative evaluation.
boundary_conditions: Claims must be factually comparable.
Relative evaluation may create credibility costs.
transport_limits: Advertising/comparison tasks strongest.

records.mechanism: Greater narrative transportation is associated with changes in evaluations/persuasive outcomes.
boundary_conditions: Narrative quality, familiarity, identification and recipient factors moderate effects.
transport_limits: Narrative messages only; not generic storytelling label.

records.mechanism: Acknowledging and refuting opposing arguments can alter perceived source/message credibility relative to one-sided structures.
boundary_conditions: Negative information amount, placement, refutation and receiver prior knowledge matter.
transport_limits: No universal superiority of two-sided messages.

records.mechanism: Audience design uses beliefs about addressee needs/knowledge to adapt linguistic and rhetorical stance.
boundary_conditions: Audience assumptions can be wrong.
Adaptation depends on communicative goal and common ground.
transport_limits: Language-production mechanism, not proof that tailoring increases persuasion.

records.mechanism: Analogical/metaphorical message mappings require receiver-side figurative/cross-domain interpretation.
boundary_conditions: Analogy is broader than metaphor.
Familiarity and complexity affect interpretation.
transport_limits: Metaphor evidence only partially supports general analogy.

records.mechanism: Self-relevance supplies top-down priority signals that can bias selective attention toward personally significant information.
boundary_conditions: Self-relevance is context and identity dependent.
Bottom-up salience can compete with self-relevance.
transport_limits: Neurocognitive review does not justify a universal marketing effect size.

records.mechanism: Affective goodness/badness evaluations provide a rapid informational input that can be used as an affect heuristic in judgment.
boundary_conditions: Affect is useful only when treated as diagnostic of the target.
Incidental affect can mislead judgment.
transport_limits: No claim that affect dominates all decisions.

records.mechanism: Promotion/prevention motivational orientation moderates persuasive response when message features are motivationally matched or mismatched.
boundary_conditions: Requires a construct-matched message manipulation.
Matching effects vary across motive types and outcomes.
transport_limits: Do not equate personalization with motivational matching.

records.mechanism: Salient social identities and accommodation goals can bias register/style choices and interpretation of socially indexed language.
boundary_conditions: Language identities are fluid and interaction-specific.
Accommodation can converge or diverge.
transport_limits: Sociolinguistic identity is not a fixed persona label.
Target register/formality node remains provisional; edge cannot exceed endpoint confidence.

records.mechanism: Evaluative lexical polarity helps construct the gain/loss meaning of a decision description and can thereby shift risky choice framing.
boundary_conditions: Reference-point and outcome-salience mechanisms must be distinguished.
Language-specific polarity and negation matter.
transport_limits: Evidence is strongest for controlled risky-choice framing tasks.

records.mechanism: Syntactic/structural complexity can alter the amount and character of message processing, thereby changing conditions for elaboration.
boundary_conditions: Complexity can increase effort or impair comprehension depending on ability and motivation.
Sentence length is not equivalent to syntactic complexity.
transport_limits: No universal claim that simpler syntax persuades better.

records.mechanism: Syntactic ambiguity increases competition/reanalysis demands and can therefore increase active processing load.
boundary_conditions: Context can resolve ambiguity early.
Prior knowledge and language proficiency matter.
transport_limits: Sentence-level processing relation; not a direct persuasion effect.

records.mechanism: Longer dependencies increase maintenance/integration demands and thereby processing load.
boundary_conditions: Language structure and predictability matter.
transport_limits: Do not convert dependency length directly into readability score.

records.mechanism: Higher linguistic surprisal tends to increase processing difficulty, reducing fluency relative to more predictable continuations.
boundary_conditions: Unexpected information can be useful or informative despite lower fluency.
Frequency and semantic fit also matter.
transport_limits: Fluency effect is not equivalent to persuasion or attention.

records.mechanism: Greater goal/issue importance increases personal involvement and motivation to process a persuasive message.
boundary_conditions: Importance may also increase defensive processing when prior attitudes are strong.
transport_limits: Do not equate involvement with agreement.

records.mechanism: Controlling or identity-threatening injunctive norms can evoke reactance and resistance.
boundary_conditions: Norm legitimacy, autonomy relevance, audience stance and wording matter.
transport_limits: Injunctive norms can also be internalized and effective.

records.mechanism: When injunctive norm pressure is experienced as controlling, it can undermine intrinsic motivation.
boundary_conditions: Internalized/valued norms need not undermine motivation.
Autonomy support changes the effect.
transport_limits: No universal anti-norm effect.

records.mechanism: A claim-support structure supplies reasons/evidence that can be evaluated for receiver-side argument strength and quality.
boundary_conditions: Well-formed structure can still support a false or weak claim.
Argument quality depends on content and audience standards.
transport_limits: Structure is not persuasion by itself.

records.mechanism: A relevant concession can alter perceived honesty/trustworthiness by acknowledging limitations, but may also expose weaknesses.
boundary_conditions: Magnitude and placement of negative information matter.
Refutation changes effects.
transport_limits: No universal credibility boost from admitting a flaw.

records.mechanism: Clear next-step specification can reduce ambiguity-related implementation burden in an action path.
boundary_conditions: Cannot remove external barriers, low motivation, or low value.
transport_limits: Design relation is plausible but direct generalizable causal effect remains under-calibrated.

records.mechanism: How a request is framed can alter compliance probability through social/normative and motivational interpretations.
boundary_conditions: Prior behavior, norm cues, reciprocity, authority and wording matter.
transport_limits: Specific request contexts; no universal wording formula.

records.mechanism: Explicitly naming an action can reduce uncertainty about what compliance would entail, while excessive pressure can trigger resistance.
boundary_conditions: Action clarity and persuasion pressure are distinct.
transport_limits: CTA explicitness is provisional and channel dependent.

records.mechanism: Emotional appeals can shift evaluative attitudes through affective/appraisal pathways.
boundary_conditions: Emotion type, intensity, relevance and audience state matter.
transport_limits: No generic emotional-vs-rational superiority.

records.mechanism: Stronger character identification can contribute to narrative-related evaluative change.
boundary_conditions: Identification is distinct from transportation and liking.
Narrative and character attributes matter.
transport_limits: Narrative persuasion contexts.
